subject: Math
subskill: Write Equation from Slope and Point
prompt: Line $j$ in the $xy$-plane is defined by $y = \frac{5}{3}x - 22$. Line $k$ is perpendicular to line $j$ and passes through the point $(3, -7)$. Which of the following equations defines line $k$?
explanation: Line $j$ has slope $\frac{5}{3}$. Since line $k$ is perpendicular to line $j$, the slope of line $k$ is the negative reciprocal of $\frac{5}{3}$, which is $-\frac{3}{5}$. Using point-slope form with $(3, -7)$: $y - (-7) = -\frac{3}{5}(x - 3)$, which simplifies to $y + 7 = -\frac{3}{5}x + \frac{9}{5}$, so $y = -\frac{3}{5}x + \frac{9}{5} - 7 = -\frac{3}{5}x + \frac{9}{5} - \frac{35}{5} = -\frac{3}{5}x - \frac{26}{5}$.
